study: Nugent et al. 2016 (Coaching Science Inquiry / CSI, R2Ed Working Paper, IES R305C090022)
eval_evidence: R2Ed (Univ. of Nebraska-Lincoln) working paper authored by the program's own research team (Nugent, Kunz, et al.) under their IES development grant; no third-party/independent evaluator. They developed CSI and evaluated it themselves.
developer_evidence: Summer institute was 'led by project coaches with support from university project faculty' and content was delivered by project coaches and science educators (p.~16); the technology-delivered coaching sessions were delivered by the project's own coaches.
cascade_evidence: Project coaches/university faculty (the research team) delivered both the summer institute and the coaching directly to the science teachers; no train-the-trainer intermediary hop.
counterfactual_evidence: Control = business-as-usual: control teachers received no summer institute and no coaching (per design/extraction record); science instruction as usual.
coaching_evidence: 8-12 technology-delivered (WebEx), ASYNCHRONOUS coaching sessions (~1-2/week) across 6-8 weeks, delivered OUTSIDE classroom instruction time via review of teacher-submitted classroom videos -> recurring but remote/video-based, not physical in-class coaching cycles; coded occasional (conservative; not the in-the-teacher's-own-classroom level required for frequent_inclass).
student_dose_evidence: Pure teacher PD; only the teachers' own science (guided-inquiry) instruction changes. No tutoring, pull-out, or added student-facing dose.
maturity_evidence: CSI is a single-year intervention (summer institute then 6-8 weeks of coaching during that school year); outcomes measured post-unit in the same year; no multi-year maturity axis (designed as a one-time PD sequence).
